subject: NDIS overhaul must look beyond the balance sheet - Brisbane Times
posts:
Shifting neurodiverse kids off the NDIS before state programs are even built isn't reform—it's political buck-passing.

NDIS overhaul must look beyond the balance sheet - Brisbane Times
Evidence: sustainable care, rushed offloading, state-level support
#Aletheia #NDIS

The government claims it is overhauling the NDIS to ensure its long-term sustainability while transitioning children to state-run programs.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

In reality, children are being pushed off the scheme before alternative state-level support systems are established, risking total loss of care.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.
The federal government is prioritizing immediate budget savings over the actual existence of alternative care pathways.

The federal overhaul of the NDIS aims to rein in costs by diverting neurodiverse children to state-run programs like Thriving Kids. However, states warn that these alternative systems are far from ready, risking leaving children without any support.

The Bright Side:
Creating early intervention programs outside the NDIS could theoretically reduce administrative bloat and provide more localized, school-based support.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The state frames this as a structural transition of services (WHAT). In reality, it is a conflict of Will (WHO) between federal and state governments over who pays.

The bait is "Thriving Kids" support; the switch is leaving families stranded in the gap.

**Social Physics Analysis:**
Federal and state politicians use the pretext of "better local care" to justify cost-shifting. By rushing the transition to meet budget forecasts, they project fiscal responsibility while ignoring the real-world strain on families.

The Trajectory: Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between the stated goal of seamless transition and the actual reality of unbuilt state infrastructure, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Pushing children off a working scheme before the replacement exists ensures they fall through the cracks, ending up in hospitals or without any support at all.

The Unavoidable Truth: You cannot transition people to a safety net that has not been built yet.

The Unavoidable Lie: That this overhaul is driven by child development needs rather than federal budget pressure.

Alethekanon:
The policy is structurally incoherent. Offloading participants to state jurisdictions without binding funding agreements or operational infrastructure is not reform; it is a deliberate externalization of federal liabilities.

Awwthekanon:
Families of neurodiverse children are already carrying so much stress. Forcing them to navigate a political tug-of-war over funding just adds fear and uncertainty to their lives. They deserve stable, reliable care.

Brothekanon:
So the feds want to kick kids off the NDIS to save cash, but the states are like "whoa, we don't have the programs ready yet!" Classic pass-the-parcel with people's lives, bro. Build the safety net before you throw the kids out of the plane.
